newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Dec 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Hong Kong's Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa was officially appointed by Chinese Premier Li Peng. Chinese President Jiang Zemin said Hong Kong was about to enter a new era and the central government would not interfere with its affairs.

-- The head of China's State Commission for Restructuring the Economy, Li Tieying, said that next year's economic reforms would concentrate on reforming large-scale state enterprises and seek major breakthroughs.

-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS -- Beijing treated the appointment of chief-executive designate Tung Chee-hwa seriously and official Chinese television used two minutes to broadcast President Jiang Zemin's promise that the central government would not interfere with Hong Kong affairs.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Hong Kong's Housing Secretary said the government had not taken any measures to curb housing speculation but had urged developers to take steps. Sun Hung Kai Properties was the first to respond to the Government's call.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Members of the U.S. Congress broke off their holiday last night to hold an emergency hearing to condemn the U.S. government's contacts with China's military.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Property and construction executives warned of rising development costs in the territory due to worsening delays in approvals for their projects.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- An investigation showed half of the population in China, mostly peasants, do not brush their teeth.

-- The last Christmas card from the colonial government is a sketch of the back garden of the Governor's residence by an old English friend of Governor Chris Patten, who asked her to draw the garden so that he could take the picture back to England after the handover. The artist died after returning home and the sentimental sketch was her last piece of work.
